drug_identity.off_label_note: Specific therapeutic dosages are generally considered extra-label or supplemental.

metabolism_and_clearance.extra_information: Essential fatty acids are an integral part of the cellular framework of all cells and help to maintain normal cellular function.

organ_burden_logic.note: Based on reported adverse effects and precautions.

brain.evidence: Rarely, some dogs may become lethargic.

blood.evidence: May affect platelet function and bleeding times; may decrease platelet activity and increase the risk of bleeding.

kidney.evidence: Used as adjunctive treatment for chronic kidney disease to decrease magnitude of proteinuria.

liver.evidence: May be beneficial for hepatic fibrosis and steatosis.

heart.evidence: Beneficial for cardiovascular disease, heart failure, dysrhythmias, and arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy.

brain.evidence: No significant feline-specific neurologic burden noted.

blood.evidence: May affect platelet function and bleeding times in cats.

kidney.evidence: Used for adjunctive treatment of kidney disease.

liver.evidence: No significant primary hepatic burden noted.

heart.evidence: Used for adjunctive treatment of CHF.

timing_profile.evidence: Prolonged periods (ie, weeks to months) are required for their actions to take effect when used for pruritus.

_ddi_note: Omega-3 fatty acids may augment the antiplatelet effect of aspirin.

drug_interactions.evidence: Potential effects on bleeding times; omega-3 fatty acids have been shown to augment the antiplatelet effect of aspirin.
May have a steroid-sparing effect in dogs with atopic dermatitis.
May have a cyclosporine-sparing effect in dogs with atopic dermatitis.
May increase the risk of bleeding.

dosage_list.duration_note: Alternatively, 200-300 mg/kg PO once daily, with a suggested upper limit of 4-5 g daily.
May be increased to the NRC safe upper limit (370 mg/kg^0.75).
Alternatively, EPA 90 mg/kg in combination with DHA 20 mg/kg PO once daily.

dosage_list.context: Inflammatory or immunologic disorders (e.g., IBD, atopy)

dosage_list.duration_note: Dosages greater than EPA + DHA 75 mg/kg^0.67 per day should be used with caution.
dosage_list.evidence: Anecdotal dosage extrapolated from human data.

dosage_list.duration_note: Practically, 1 capsule (approx 180mg EPA / 120mg DHA) per 4.5 kg (10 lb) body weight.

renal_dose_adjustment.note: Used as an adjunctive treatment for chronic kidney disease to decrease the magnitude of proteinuria.

hepatic_dose_adjustment.note: May be beneficial for hepatic fibrosis and steatosis.

effects_and_mechanisms.common_mechanism: Affects arachidonic acid concentrations in plasma lipids and cellular membranes, and affects the degree of inflammatory prostaglandins, leukotrienes, and thromboxane production.
common_extra_effects: GI distress (belching, vomiting, diarrhea) at high doses

species_notes.dog: Dosages often determined using metabolic weight (kg^0.75) and combined weight of EPA/DHA. Omega-3 supplementation may reduce the incidence of lipemic aqueous in miniature schnauzers.
species_notes.cat: Less evidence supporting safety and efficacy in cats than in dogs. Dosages greater than EPA + DHA 75 mg/kg^0.67 per day should be used with caution.

dog.evidence: Use with caution in patients with primary or secondary hemostatic disorders, previous bouts of pancreatitis, or protracted diarrhea.

cat.evidence: Use caution with primary/secondary hemostatic disorders. Dosages > 75 mg/kg^0.67 per day should be used with caution and under veterinary supervision.

storage_and_forms.storage: Products should be stored in an airtight container in a cool, dry place, protected from heat, light, and air as fatty acids are susceptible to oxidation and breakdown.

section_1_2_10.highlights: Most commonly used orally for adjunctive treatment of pruritus associated with inflammatory skin conditions in dogs and cats. May be useful as an anti-inflammatory for chronic conditions (e.g., CKD, osteoarthritis). May affect platelet function and bleeding times.
section_1_2_10.indications: Adjunctive treatment of pruritus (atopy, idiopathic seborrhea, miliary dermatitis, eosinophilic granuloma complex). Adjunctive anti-inflammatory treatment for CKD, arthritis, cardiovascular disease, IBD, hepatic fibrosis, steatosis, neoplastic diseases. Lower airway disease in horses.
section_1_2_10.client_info: Treatment for itching may require 2 to 3 months to see effectiveness. Upset stomach and loose stools are the most common side effects. Some animals may bruise or bleed more easily.
